name: Fray Island
summary: Warriors gather on Fray Island, just off the Merchant Coast of the Barrens. The rocky islet holds a rough training ring where fighters from across Azeroth test their skill.

sections.title: A Proving Ground for Brawlers
sections.body: Fray Island lies off the eastern bluffs of the Barrens, beyond the watchful eyes of Orgrimmar and Theramore. Warriors of every race and creed train here. At the island's heart, Klannoc Macleod oversees a fighting arena where seasoned fighters and raw recruits meet in brutal brawls.

sections.title: The Trial of the Affray
sections.body: The ring on Fray Island follows a simple code of martial combat, despite the hostile waters around it. Warriors come at their trainers' direction to face The Affray, a grueling gauntlet against waves of challengers that ends with a bout against champion Big Will. Here, Horde and Alliance allegiance gives way to strength and martial discipline.

faq.q: What is Fray Island used for?
faq.answer: Fray Island is a training ground for warriors and the site of The Affray, a brutal combat trial. Warriors from both factions come to test their endurance and master advanced stances.
No kingdom or faction rules Fray Island. Warriors of every race and creed train there, and Klannoc Macleod oversees the combat ring.

faq.q: How do I reach Fray Island?
aliases: how to get to fray island
faq.answer: Fray Island lies in the Great Sea, off the Barrens' eastern coast and south of Ratchet. Reaching it means swimming a long way from shore through waters filled with sharks and frenzy.
The Affray is an endurance trial held in Fray Island's fighting cage. A warrior stands atop the grate and defeats successive waves of challengers before facing brawler Big Will.

angles.text: As a warrior, you can test your discipline and strength at Fray Island's training ground. Klannoc Macleod and The Affray test whether you can adopt the Berserker Stance.
Klannoc Macleod is human, but the warriors who gather in his ring share a bond of combat across racial lines.
